standard_prerequisites: enumerable sets as W_e, the domain-range description of enumerations
unbounded minimization producing partial computable functions
core_obligations: Prove that S is computably enumerable iff S = { x : exists y R(x,y) } for some computable relation R
proof_roadmap: Forward: if S is c.e. then S = W_e for some index e, and S = { x : exists y T(e,x,y) } by the definition of W_e in terms of the T predicate
Reverse: given S = { x : exists y R(x,y) } with R computable, the partial function f(x) = least y with R(x,y) is partial computable by unbounded minimization
S is exactly the domain of f, and domains of partial computable functions are computably enumerable
difficulty_reason: Both directions are short and written out; the substance is the standard identification of c.e. sets with positive existential definitions.
